newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan sets up institution for failed credit unions.
newsitem.headline: Japan sets up institution for failed credit unions.

text.p: The Resolution and Collection Bank Ltd (RCB) was set up on Monday to handle bankruptcies of credit unions over the past two years and to deal with possible future failures of such financial institutions.

The new bank will take over and wind up failed credit unions after paying back deposits and recovering assets over the next five years until the end of March 2001, Shigeru Mizuno, the president of the bank, said.
"It is a difficult task to recover (problem loans) but it is unavoidable and we will try hard to do so," he told reporters.
Credit unions are small financial institutions which take deposits and lend mainly to members.

Parliament passed financial bills in June to reorganise Tokyo Kyodo Bank, which was originally set up in January 1995 to take over the assets and business of two failed credit unions in Tokyo. Tokyo Kyodo also took over the assets of another Tokyo-based credit union, Cosmo, which collapsed in July last year.

As well its headquarters in Tokyo, the RCB will set up another office in Osaka to deal more effectively with credit union failures in western Japan. The bank is expected to take over the assets of Kizu Shinyo Kumiai and Osaka Shinyo Kumiai, Osaka-based credit unions which collapsed last year.

To cope with possible future collapses at other credit unions, the Deposit Insurance Corp of Japan (DIC) decided last week to inject 120 billion yen into the RCB to boost its capital to 160 billion yen. The DIC, which was set up to protect depositors from bank failures, will also guarantee up to 338.5 billion yen worth of loans to the new bank.
The government will provide the necessary money from the state budget if needed, a RCB official said.
The RCB is expected to be dissolved in 2006, he said.
